cards.text: Paul is writing to the believers in Colossae. He tells them they've been raised with Christ. So now he says: here's where you aim.

cards.question: Since the Colossians have been raised with Christ, what does Paul tell them to strive for?

cards.text: Up above is where Christ is seated, at the right hand of God, and Paul says set your minds on things above, not on earthly things. Friend, I spent YEARS in a junk drawer staring at the bottom of a takeout menu, so trust me, looking UP is an upgrade.

cards.question: Paul tells the Colossians they died, and now their life is hidden with ___ in God.
Paul calls Christ their life. When Christ appears, what happens to the believers?

answers.text: They appear with Him in glory
They are tested one last time
They are sent out to the nations

cards.text: Then Paul gets serious. Put to death the parts of your earthly nature: sexual immorality, impurity, lust, evil desires and greed.

cards.question: In that list of things to put to death, Paul calls greed idolatry.

cards.text: Paul says that because of these things, the wrath of God is coming on the sons of disobedience.

cards.question: Paul says the Colossian believers never walked in those ways.

cards.text: But now Paul has a second list of things to put aside, and this one's about how you treat people and what comes out of your mouth. Friend, somebody needs to pin this list to the top of the office group chat.

cards.question: Which of these is on Paul's second list of things the Colossians must put aside?

cards.text: Next up: don't lie to one another. And Paul's reason sounds like he's talking about getting dressed.

cards.question: Paul says don't lie to one another, because you've taken off the old ___ with its practices.

cards.text: And they've put on the new self, which is being renewed. It's like trading a crusty, flour-caked apron for a clean one, and friend, NOBODY takes off the crusty one just to put it right back ON.

cards.question: Paul says the new self is being renewed in knowledge. In whose image?
Paul says that in the new self, Greek and Jew, slave and free still stand in separate groups.

cards.text: Here, Paul says, there's no Greek or Jew, circumcised or uncircumcised, barbarian, Scythian, slave or free. Christ is all and is in all.
Paul's still talking clothes. Since they're the elect of God, holy and beloved, he's handing them a whole new outfit to put on.

cards.question: What does Paul tell God's elect to clothe themselves with?

cards.text: Humility, gentleness and patience go on too. Then Paul says bear with one another, which is Bible for: that coworker who hits reply-all on EVERY email? Yeah. Bear with them.

cards.question: Paul says to forgive a complaint against someone only after they make it right.

cards.text: Forgive any complaint, Paul says, as the Lord forgave you. And then one last piece goes on over the whole outfit.

cards.question: Over all these virtues, Paul says to put on ___, which is the bond of perfect unity.

cards.text: Next, let the peace of Christ rule in your hearts. And Paul tacks three little words on the end: “And be thankful.”

cards.question: Paul gives a reason to let the peace of Christ rule in their hearts. What is it?

answers.text: They were called to it as one body
It keeps their enemies far away
It earns them the favor of God

cards.text: Then Paul says let the word of Christ richly dwell within you. Not visit, not drop by on weekends, DWELL, like it moved in and unpacked.

cards.question: As the word of Christ richly dwells in them, Paul has the believers teaching and admonishing one another.

cards.text: Paul tells them to let that word dwell in them as they sing psalms, hymns and spiritual songs with gratitude in their hearts to God. Then Paul throws the widest net he's got: whatever you do, in word or deed, WHATEVER, from sitting in traffic to stamping cookie number four hundred.

cards.question: What does Paul tell the believers to do with whatever they do, in word or deed?

answers.text: Do it all in the name of the Lord Jesus
Do it all by the rules of the elders
Do it all where the church can see

cards.question: Paul tells them to give thanks to God the Father through the Lord Jesus.

findings.problem: Paul shows up for the first time in the walkthrough, but the card never says who he is. It only says he is writing to the believers in Colossae.

rule.text: **New people.** The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The blank asks the baker to supply the exact word in Paul's phrase "taken off the old ___" (self, house or name). Nothing before this card introduces the idea of an "old self." Card 12 only hints at getting dressed, so the card tests wording the baker hasn't seen rather than meaning they can reason out.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.
